first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ, and two independent archived memories (memory_31: signup simplification lifted SMB activation; memory_86: shortened onboarding lifted completion and time-to-value) directly support addressing this with low downstream risk to revenue quality — unlike promotional pricing, which chases the competitor's price war and risks attracting low-LTV, price-sensitive accounts that could erode sustainable qualified revenue even if memory_73 shows short-term acquisition lift. Activation is also down 6%, and onboarding improvements plausibly feed into activation, giving this experiment compounding value versus a narrower activation_messaging test. I'm verifying memory_31 and memory_86 because they are the two oldest/most consolidated inputs underpinning this choice and because their original experiment conditions (segment, definition of 'completion', time window) matter for judging whether the prior lift still applies to a self-serve SMB base now facing competitive pressure. I am deliberately not spending verification budget on memory_73 (promotional pricing) because I am not selecting that action this cycle, though I flag it as a plausible but riskier alternative worth re-examining if onboarding fixes don't stem SMB losses. Scale is standard_experiment rather than broad_rollout because, despite two supportive memories, current market conditions (competitor pricing shock) are a confound that could interact with onboarding changes in ways prior sessions didn't observe.

final.rationale: Verified records confirm both memories: exp_31 (signup simplification) showed activation +9% and qualified revenue +4% on SMB, but also a small -1% dip in 30-day retention, noted as confirmed only for SMB and not replicated elsewhere. exp_86 (shortened onboarding) showed completion +13%, time-to-value -2.1 days, and retention +3%, fully confirmed with no revenue figure reported. Together these support simplify_onboarding as the best current lever: it directly targets the two observed weaknesses (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) with mechanisms that have empirical backing, unlike promotional_pricing, which risks accelerating a race-to-the-bottom against the competitor's aggressive entry pricing and attracting low-quality, price-sensitive revenue rather than sustainable qualified revenue. I flag downstream_value_risk because exp_31's -1% retention effect, even though small and offset by revenue lift, means the onboarding-simplification path is not free of tradeoffs, and the original scope was SMB-specific and not shown to generalize — an important caveat before any broad rollout. Given this, I keep the experiment at standard_experiment scale rather than broad_rollout, allowing us to observe activation, completion, and short-term retention/revenue signals in the current market context (competitor pricing pressure could change customer mix and interact with the effect sizes seen previously). This preserves the qualified-revenue objective without conflating a genuine funnel improvement with an unvalidated response to competitive pricing dynamics.
